than 5% of the examined fields (figure 2b ). immunohistochemistry demonstrated strong nuclear oct3/4 immunoreactivity (figure 3b ) and diffuse membranous cd117 positivity (figure 3c ). its distinct anatomical location, together with the long latency period following successful treatment, supports the diagnosis of a metachronous intracranial germinoma. discussion cns germinomas typically arise in midline structures and occur predominantly in young patients. despite their malignant nature, they demonstrate remarkable radiosensitivity, achieving disease control rates exceeding 90% with current radiotherapy protocols . their predilection for the pineal and suprasellar regions explains the high incidence of obstructive hydrocephalus and intracranial hypertension at presentation . although overall prognosis is excellent, a relevant proportion of patients develop late complications, particularly endocrine dysfunction such as hypopituitarism and growth hormone deficiency related to irradiation of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis. neurocognitive sequelae have also been reported, supporting the need for long-term, multidisciplinary follow-up . unlike many other intracranial tumors, germinomas are frequently managed without upfront surgical resection because of their characteristic radiological appearance, supportive tumor marker profile, deep midline location, and marked radiosensitivity. surgical intervention is generally reserved for csf diversion in patients with hydrocephalus, tissue diagnosis when the diagnosis is uncertain, or management of residual or recurrent disease. this approach has achieved excellent long-term disease control while minimizing the morbidity associated with surgery in deep-seated lesions . although most recurrences occur within the first several years after treatment, late recurrences have been reported, underscoring the importance of lifelong vigilance . the uniqueness of this case lies not only in the prolonged disease-free interval but also in the development of a metachronous periventricular germinoma without radiological evidence of residual or recurrent disease at the primary pineal site. published reports indicate that germinomas typically recur within previously irradiated fields or within the same ventricular compartment. recurrences arising in distant, previously uninvolved sites are far less common and almost never appear beyond 10 years of follow-up . thus, the emergence of a new periventricular mass 13 years after initial diagnosis and following a prolonged tumor-free interval represents one of the most atypical patterns described for this disease. this biochemical profile favors the diagnosis of a new lesion of identical cellular lineage rather than a late recurrence of the original tumor. metachronous germ cell tumors, defined as new germ cell neoplasms arising after a prolonged disease-free interval, are exceptionally rare and generally occur much earlier than in this case. diagnosis in this patient required integrating clinical symptoms, neuroimaging, and biomarker analysis. the heterogeneous enhancement pattern and periventricular distribution on mri broadened the differential diagnosis, which included primary cns lymphoma, high-grade glioma, metastatic disease, ependymal tumors, inflammatory or demyelinating lesions, and recurrent germinoma. among these entities, primary cns lymphoma was considered the leading alternative diagnosis because of the lesion's deep periventricular location and marked metabolic activity on pet. in the absence of a definitive radiologic pattern and given the nonspecific tumor marker profile, histopathological examination was essential to establish the diagnosis. histopathologic examination demonstrated classic germinoma features, including nests of tumor cells separated by thin fibrovascular septa and prominent perivascular lymphocytic infiltrates . immunohistochemical positivity for oct4 and cd117 further supported the diagnosis, as both markers are sensitive and specific for germinomatous tumors. this case emphasizes the need for continued long-term surveillance, even after complete remission, due to the possibility, albeit low, of metachronous germ cell neoplasms. it also highlights the importance of comprehensive diagnostic evaluation when imaging or clinical presentation is atypical. conclusions this case illustrates the typical initial course of a pineal germinoma while emphasizing that, even after complete response to radiotherapy, patients remain at risk for late endocrine sequelae and, in rare cases, metachronous germ cell tumors. the development of a new lesion in a distinct anatomical location more than a decade after initial treatment highlights the limitations of short-term surveillance strategies. in cns germinomas, long periods of clinical and radiological stability do not exclude the possibility of late tumor emergence. therefore, prolonged, multidisciplinary follow-up with sustained clinical vigilance is essential, particularly when new neurological or radiological changes arise, regardless of the time elapsed since primary therapy. disclosures human theoretical contributions the contributions outlined in this section represent conceptual and theoretical advances proposed by the authors to integrate existing evidence through the com-b framework, rather than empirically derived clinical algorithms. this review's innovation lies in transforming the com-b model from descriptive tool to intervention design framework. relative to existing reviews, this review's specific contributions are threefold. first, it moves beyond descriptive factor listing to operationalize the com-b framework as an intervention design tool, explicitly mapping bcts to dimensional targets rather than using com-b solely as a post-hoc classification scheme. second, it integrates device-level evidence (sitt versus mitt) with patient-level behavioral analysis, demonstrating how regimen simplification operates through the opportunity dimension while acknowledging that opportunity optimization alone is insufficient without concurrent capability and motivation support. third, it proposes a phenotype-stratified intervention model that translates theoretical dimensions into clinically actionable matching rules, pending empirical validation. these contributions are conceptual and organizational rather than empirical; they synthesize existing evidence through a novel theoretical lens to generate testable hypotheses for future research. clinical and quality of life in bariatric surgery candidates with morbid obesity regarding the onset of the weight problem in childhood, adolescence, or adulthood. materials and methods we included 453 patients who applied to our center for preoperative bariatric surgery assessment between january 2010 and april 2019. we reviewed the sociodemographic information, psychiatric diagnoses, and results of the body shape questionnaire-34, quality of life scale, beck depression inventory, and beck anxiety inventory of all patients. results concerns about weight and body shape were increased in women (p 0.001), unemployed patients (p = 0.001), those with a comorbid psychiatric disorder (p 0.001), and those with childhood- or adolescent-onset of weight problems (r = -0.170; p 0.001). concerns about weight and body shape had a relationship with the vitality (r = -0.434), mental health (r = -0.464), social functioning (r = -0.418), pain (r = -0.307), and general health (r = -0.352) subscale scores of quality of life. physical functioning was higher (p = 0.037) in patients with childhood- or adolescent-onset obesity compared to patients with adult-onset obesity, while mental health was higher (p = 0.001) in the latter group. individuals with childhood- or adolescent-onset obesity inquired about bariatric surgery options at an earlier age (p 0.001). conclusion while performing routine psychiatric evaluations before bariatric surgery, it is important to consider parameters such as the patient's physical functioning, level of concerns about the body, and age of onset of obesity. introduction morbid obesity is the most severe condition of obesity and can lead to both medical and social problems. these patients frequently present with psychiatric disorders as well as medical conditions. they are adversely affected by accompanying psychiatric disorders, medical conditions, failed weight-loss attempts, and social pressures to lose weight. quality of life (qol) also decreases with the high anxiety levels triggered by monitoring one's body and engaging in avoidance behaviors. studies have suggested a decrease in qol with increased body mass index (bmi) levels . low qol was reported as the major reason for preferring the bariatric surgery method among patients with morbid obesity . bmi has had a significant impact on body dissatisfaction in studies about body perception in people with obesity , and patients with obesity were found to be more dissatisfied with their bodies than nonobese individuals . more than 80% of women had negative body image in a study conducted using the body shape questionnaire (bsq) with women with obesity who were undergoing therapy due to their negative body perceptions . body dissatisfaction severity in women with obesity was more associated with perceived body weight than actual body weight . studies indicate that many factors adversely affect body perception in individuals with obesity. one study reported that slightly overweight women had the same attitudes toward their physical appearances as individuals with obesity . the study's hypotheses were as follows: h1: it is hypothesized that being female and having a psychiatric comorbidity are significant predictors of elevated concerns about body shape and weight in patients awaiting bariatric surgery. h2: there will be a significant difference in body-image concerns based on the timing of obesity onset, with early-onset individuals exhibiting higher levels of weight-related distress than their adult-onset counterparts. h3: early-onset obesity is associated with an earlier age of seeking bariatric surgery. h4: surgery candidates with adult-onset obesity will demonstrate higher physical function scores and fewer obesity-related comorbidities than candidates with childhood- or adolescent-onset obesity. materials and methods in our center, we carry out routine medical examinations of patients who are admitted to our clinic with the hope of undergoing bariatric surgery. these patients are evaluated in a multidisciplinary manner by endocrinologists, general surgeons, dietitians, psychiatrists, cardiologists, pulmonologists, physical medicine practitioners, and rehabilitation physicians. during the preoperative psychological evaluation, the patients are examined regarding their understanding of the surgical procedure, decision-making, and postoperative adjustment and management skills. current psychiatric disorders are documented at the baseline interview by trained clinicians (master's level or higher) using the structured clinical interview for dsm-iv-tr axis i disorders . data on eating disorders that may play a role in the etiology of obesity were excluded from the analysis of this study due to missing data in the records. the study was approved by the bulent ecevit university clinical studies ethics committee on 22 may 2019 with approval number 2019/08. sociodemographic information we reviewed demographic information such as age, sex, marital and educational status, occupation, alcohol consumption, smoking status, and other medical conditions of the patients. data were collected regarding the patients' family history of psychiatric disorders and obesity, diet history, exercise history, daily screen time, and the onset and duration of the weight problem. to define age at the onset of obesity, we used the categories of "childhood-adolescent onset (5-17 years)" and "adult onset (18+ years)." we estimated the duration of obesity by asking the participants. body mass index (bmi) bmi was calculated as weight (kg) divided by height (m 2 ). short form-36 (sf-36) we used the turkish version of the sf-36, which consists of the 8 subscales of physical functioning, physical role limitations, emotional role limitations, vitality, mental health, social functioning, pain, and general health perceptions. every subscale is scored in the range of 0 to 100. higher scores indicate better health and higher levels of functioning . beck depression inventory (bdi) developed by beck et al., this self-report scale consists of 21 questions to assess the severity of depression symptoms . it is a 4-point likert-type scale with scores ranging from 0 to 63. beck anxiety inventory (bai) developed by beck et al., this self-assessment scale consists of 21 questions . the total score ranges from 0 to 23, with higher scores reflecting a greater level of anxiety severity. carried out the turkish validity and reliability study of the scale . body shape questionnaire (bsq) data on body image was obtained using the bsq, which measures concerns about the individual's weight and body shape. developed the scale in 1987 and determined its reliability . determined the validity and reliability of the turkish version of the scale . the bsq is a one-dimensional scale containing 34 items scored with 1-6 points (1: "never," 2: "rarely," 3: "sometimes," 4: "often," 5: "very often," and 6: "always"). a score of 80 indicates no anxiety while increasing scores indicate higher levels of engagement with body image and weight and greater anxiety. the cronbach alpha internal reliability and consistency coefficient was 0.88 for the scale. statistics spss 18.0 (spss inc., chicago, il, usa) was used for statistical evaluation. the shapiro-wilk test was used to test whether the numerical variables were normally distributed. the chi-square test was used for the analysis of differences and the relationships between groups regarding categorical variables. when the data met the assumptions of the parametric test in the comparison of two groups regarding numerical variables, we used hypothesis testing of the difference between the means of the two groups, and we used the mann-whitney u test when those assumptions were not met. we used pearson correlation analysis when our data met the assumptions of the parametric test of the linear relationship between two numerical variables and we used spearman correlation analysis when those assumptions were not met. the confidence interval was 95% and values of p 0.05 were considered significant. results of all bariatric surgery candidates in our hospital, 320 (70.6%) were women and 133 (29.4%) were men. according to the sociodemographic evaluations, 41.7% of the patients were primary school graduates, 72% were married, and 49% were housewives or unemployed. adult and childhood-adolescent onset had occurred for 53.2%, and 46.8% of the patients, respectively. while 69.8% reported that they had tried diets that did not work, 10.2% had a history of laxative use. half of the patients indicated that they did not do any exercise, 18.3% reported exercising regularly, and 31.1% reported exercising irregularly. furthermore, 28.7% had a psychiatric disorder, the most frequent of which were major depression, anxiety disorder, and adjustment disorder. we did not observe any suicidal thoughts in these patients during our examinations; however, 3.1% of the patients had a history of attempted suicide. the distributions of psychiatric diagnoses and scores of the patients are shown in table 2 . the relationships between bsq scores and sociodemographic and descriptive characteristics are shown in table 3 . the mean bsq score of women was significantly higher than that of men (p 0.001). the bsq scores of the unemployed/housewife group were significantly higher than those of the employed group (p = 0.001). the mean bsq score of the group with psychiatric disorders was significantly higher than that of the group without any psychiatric disorders (p 0.001). significant negative correlations were found between age and duration of the weight problem and bsq scores (respectively r = -0.137, p = 0.004; r = -0.170, p 0.001). there were also negative correlations between bsq scores and all sf-36 subscale scores ( table 4 ). however, there was no significant relationship between bmi and bsq scores (r = 0.064, p 0.05). when comparing the demographic characteristics of the participants based on the onset of obesity, statistically significant differences were found between the groups in terms of marital status (p 0.001), occupation (p = 0.001), presence of physical disorder (p = 0.027), and daily exercise duration (p = 0.005). among those whose obesity began in adulthood, the rates of being married and having a physical disorder were higher. bonferroni-corrected post hoc comparisons revealed significant differences according to the timing of obesity onset. specifically, the proportion of students was higher among participants with childhood-adolescent onset of obesity compared to those with adult-onset obesity (p 0.05). distinct patterns were also observed in physical activity: the group with childhood-adolescent onset exhibited a significantly higher frequency of daily exercise lasting 30-60 min, whereas the group with adult onset was significantly more likely to report no exercise at all (p 0.05). in contrast, no statistically significant differences were identified between the groups for sex, psychiatric diagnosis, laxative use, or dietary habits (p 0.05). differences in scale scores and numerical data between the groups according to the time of onset of the weight problem are shown in table 5 . individuals with childhood- or adolescent-onset sought bariatric surgery options at earlier ages (p 0.001). predictably, a relationship was found between earlier onset of obesity and longer duration of obesity. no difference was found between the two groups regarding bmi values (p = 0.631). individuals with early-onset obesity (childhood or adolescent onset) demonstrated significantly higher bsq scores than their adult-onset counterparts. the independent variables in the model explained approximately 28.5% of the variance in bsq scores. discussion although morbid obesity is widely known to reduce individual qol, it is controversial whether factors such as physical health, mental health, self-confidence, and relationships with others have any impact on this reduction . the present study found that weight and body shape concerns in role of sleep disorders as a contributing factor to impairments in cardiovascular health, neurocognitive function, and health-related quality of life in individuals with chd. methods a narrative review was conducted across pubmed, ovid, and cochrane library (1990-2025) searches for studies cross-referencing "congenital heart disease" or "fontan circulation" with sleep-related terms. inclusion criteria were studies in chd populations using objective or self-report sleep assessments; exclusions included non-english, non-original data, or conference abstracts. references of included articles were also screened to identify additional potentially relevant articles. thirty three of 523 articles screened met inclusion criteria. results sdb is prevalent in both children and adults with chd, with reported rates ranging from 31 to 63% in adults and up to 57% in children. both obstructive and central sleep apnea are observed. comorbid sdb is associated with increased inpatient mortality in infants, poorer quality of life in children and adults, neurocognitive impairments, and increased cardiovascular risk including arrhythmias and paradoxical emboli. evidence for effective treatment remains limited, though lifestyle, behavioral, and ventilation strategies show potential benefit. discussion sdb is common in both children and adults with chd and has a negative association with around 97% of infants with chd survive to age 18, and, 75% live to age 60 years ( dellborg, 2024 ). two thirds of the population with chd are adults now ( dellborg, 2024 ). despite these improvements in life expectancy, people with chd experience various long-term comorbidities. chd is associated with increased risk and younger age of onset for cardiovascular diseases, especially heart failure and stroke . arrhythmias are also prevalent among individuals with chd, which predisposes them to thromboembolic events . beyond cardiovascular comorbidities, chd is associated with neurodevelopmental and neurocognitive dysfunction. this manifests as motor and language deficits during infancy and early childhood, which can persist into adulthood, contributing to cognitive impairment and increased risk of early-onset dementia . chd also negatively impacts mental health, and lifetime prevalence of mood and anxiety disorders among individuals with chd could be as high as 50% . given the significant impact of long-term comorbidities in individuals with chd, efforts have been made to understand their pathogenesis and clinical outcomes. recent studies suggest that sleep-disordered breathing (sdb) may contribute to the development of cardiovascular and neurocognitive complications in people with chd. obstructive sleep apnea (osa) is the most common type of sdb and involves repeated airway collapse during sleep . compared to the general population, individuals with chd have higher rates of osa as a result of multiple mechanisms ( cotts et al., 2014 ; drake et al., 2020 ; harada et al., 2019 ; miles et al., 2016 ; momcilovic et al., 2024 ; sawatari et al., 2015 ; stevans et al., 2020 ). central sleep apnea (csa), a less common form of sdb characterized by improper neural control of breathing, also may be more common among individuals with chd . it is well-known that sdb contributes to significant morbidity and mortality. through repeated episodes of intermittent hypoxia and reoxygenation, sdb increases sympathetic activation, oxidative stress, and systemic inflammation, which contributes to the development of cardiovascular disease and structural brain damage . in individuals with chd, sdb may exacerbate pre-existing anatomic vulnerabilities; therefore, their effect on this population warrants careful evaluation. in this review, we examine the prevalence and impact of sdb in individuals with chd as well as management of sdb in individuals with chd. methods we conducted a narrative review of the available literature addressing sleep disorders in the chd population, with specific attention to sdb. we identified relevant articles to include in the review based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria. inclusion criteria: study performed in individuals with chd; study used objective or self-report tools to assess sdb. exclusion criteria included articles in another language than english; not an original study containing original data (no protocol articles, conference abstracts, or theses). two authors screened the titles and abstracts of all identified records to exclude studies that did not meet the eligibility criteria. any disagreements were resolved by consensus. a total of 523 articles were screened, 56 articles initially identified, and 33 articles met inclusion criteria and are included in this review ( figure 1 ). given the narrative nature of this review, the review was not prospectively registered in prospero. additionally, given the goal of providing a broad overview of all available studies on sdb in people with chd and the significant heterogeneity of studies preventing quantitative analysis across studies, no risk of bias assessment was performed. results sleep phenotypes observed in individuals with chd (2020) found a high prevalence of sdb and significant correlation between low baseline o2 saturation and apnea-hypopnea index (ahi; measure of sdb severity), further enhancing adverse outcomes as it pertains to sdb. interestingly, bmi and age, which are major risk factors for sdb in the general population, were not significantly correlated with sdb severity in this cohort, suggesting that there are other important factors related to sdb pathogenesis in individuals with fontan circulation. for instance, chronically decreased cardiac output and elevated central venous pressure can result in lower-extremity edema that redistributes to the neck when laying supine and increase risk for airway obstruction during sleep. furthermore, individuals with fontan circulation rely on passive blood flow from the vena cava to the lungs, so they are especially sensitive to increased pulmonary vascular resistance (pvr), a common effect of sdb-induced hypoxia . this may explain why individuals with lower baseline o2 saturation, and thus higher pvr have more severe sdb. higher rates of sdb have also been observed in individuals with d-transposition of the great arteries (d-tga) post-atrial switch procedure and those with chronic pulmonary regurgitation . like with fontan circulation, the interaction between these lesions and sdb may be reciprocal: cardiovascular dysfunction increases risk of sdb, which in turn worsens the lesion complications. since the "weaker" morphologic right ventricle serves as the systemic ventricle in d-tga after atrial switch, it is especially susceptible to systolic and diastolic dysfunction, and the resulting pulmonary edema can increase risk for sdb. furthermore, the morphologic left ventricle, which supports pulmonic circulation in d-tga, is susceptible to atrial-ventricular desynchrony . this can further contribute to pulmonary vascular congestion, which may compound the increased pvr caused by sdb. a similar phenomenon may occur in individuals with pulmonic regurgitation, as right-sided volume overload can compound the vasoconstrictive effects of sdb on the pulmonary circulation . notably, individuals with pfo are more likely to display symptoms of osa at a younger age and have more frequent oxygen desaturations during respiratory disturbances, possibly due to shunting of deoxygenated blood from the right to left atrium during sleep . observed that a larger pfo is associated with a higher degree of nocturnal desaturation, further supporting the hypothesis that right-to-left shunting exacerbates the hypoxemic consequences of osa . overall, chd may increase the likelihood of sdb through a variety of lesion-dependent mechanisms, including fluid overload and right-to-left shunting. clinical consequences of sleep disordered breathing in chd sdb impacts clinical outcomes across the lifespan of people with chd. in a retrospective cross-sectional study of inpatient infants with chd, the presence of sdb was associated with higher total charges, longer inpatient stay, and increased mortality risk . after infancy, sdb may continue to affect development and function in children with chd. a retrospective cross-sectional study of children with fontan circulation found that unspecified sleep disturbances were associated with lower health-related quality of life and increased risk of attention problems, anxiety, and depression . another study found that children with chd and osa scored significantly lower on memory and iq tests compared to their counterparts without osa . in addition to neurodevelopmental problems, sdb may also impact cardiovascular function in children with chd. (2006) observed that children with chd who have a positive screen for sdb experience a higher cardiovascular symptom burden, especially palpitations and exercise intolerance. (2025) found a significant association between sleep quality and adaptive functioning children with chd but not healthy controls, suggesting that sleep may be especially critical for this population. for individuals with chd, the clinical consequences of sdb persist into adulthood, manifesting as increased risk for cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease. sdb can compound the effects of pre-existing lesions; for instance, sleep apnea may promote right-to-left shunting through pfos, increasing risk of paradoxical emboli and stroke ( beelke et al., 2002 ; kar, 2014 ; pellaton et al., 2011 ). additionally, studies have found that osa is an independent risk factor for arrhythmias such as atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter in adults with chd ( escudero-martinez et al., 2023 ; jame and barnes, 2020 ; loomba et al., 2017 ; vyas et al., 2024 ). this may further compromise the underlying cardiac dysfunction, worsening the stasis of blood within the heart and promoting thromboembolism formation. sdb in adults with chd is also associated with diabetes, hypertension, and obesity, which all impair cardiovascular and cerebrovascular function . overall, available evidence suggests that the clinical consequences of sdb overlap with and may compound the effects of congenital cardiac lesions across childhood and adulthood, which can be seen in figure 2 . chd leads to various forms of cardiovascular dysfunction, such as dependent edema, pulmonary congestion, and nocturnal hypoxia, which may promote the development of sdb or exacerbate its effects. in turn, the downstream effects of sdb may compound the underlying cardiovascular dysfunction from chd. however, it is important to note that most of the existing literature on sdb in the setting of chd is observational or cross-sectional, limiting the ability to establish causal relationships between sdb and adverse outcomes in individuals with chd. sdb therapeutic considerations in select populations with chd due to altered cardiac anatomy and resulting physiologic changes, treatment of sdb in individuals with some forms of chd may be significantly more complex than sdb treatment for the general population. for instance, individuals with fontan circulation lack a sub pulmonary ventricle and are especially sensitive to increases in intrathoracic pressure caused by continuous positive airway pressure (cpap), the gold standard therapy for osa. specifically, cpap leads to increased intrathoracic pressure resulting in increased pulmonary resistance, leading to decreased systemic ventricular preload. as cardiac output in fontan circulation is exquisitely preload dependent, the increased intrathoracic pressure and increased pulmonary vascular resistance caused by cpap can reduce systemic cardiac output. case reports have reported success in using cardiac catheterization, echocardiography, and peripheral venous pressure monitoring to identify a maximum tolerated cpap pressure, which can guide treatment for individuals with fontan circulation . thus, individuals with chd can benefit from standard therapies for sdb, such as cpap, but it is important to individualize treatment parameters according to their physiology. in addition to ventilation strategies, several studies have also investigated the effects of lesion repair in improving sdb for people with chd, particularly those with pfo. since pfo and other forms of right-to-left shunting may exacerbate sdb, investigators have proposed shunt closure as a potential therapeutic strategy. (2015) observed a significant decrease in osa severity as measured by apnea-hypopnea index (ahi) after transcatheter pfo closure. (2013) did not find a significant reduction in ahi after pfo closure compared to baseline, though the former did find a decrease in subjective sleepiness. lesion repair may improve sdb in selected individuals, but the results are inconsistent, suggesting that non-anatomic factors such as ventilatory control and upper-airway physiology may also contribute to the development of sdb in individuals with chd. discussion sleep disorders are a prevalent but heterogenous comorbidity in children and adults with chd. both children and adults have demonstrated higher rates of sdb compared to the general population. notably, individuals with chd exhibit wider variation in sdb presentation. while osa accounts for the vast majority of sdb in the general population, a significant proportion of individuals with chd have csa or nocturnal hypoxemia without apnea. some associations between sdb and chd are straightforward, such as nocturnal hypoxemia in individuals with mixing of systemic and pulmonary circulation leading to a low baseline oxygen saturation. however, the literature examining specific chd lesions and sdb is mixed with studies showing limited or conflicting associations. larger studies are needed to evaluate the underlying mechanisms that appear to increase risk for sdb in people with chd. one potential mechanism of the increased risk for sdb is that underlying defects in neural crest cell migration underlie both craniofacial developmental abnormalities and chd ( keyte and hutson, 2012 ). neural crest cells are critical to brain, craniofacial and heart development. therefore, it is possible that individuals with the phenotype of chd may also have underlying craniofacial abnormalities predisposing them to sdb. consistent with this, prior literature has shown that airway anomalies are common on autopsy in children with chd and an analysis of an administrative dataset found that airway anomalies were reported 20 times more frequently in admitted infants with single ventricle chd compared to admitted infants without chd . the wide-ranging physical and mental consequences of sleep disorders are well documented and may be particularly detrimental for people with chd who are already at risk for health problems, poor quality of life and neurodevelopmental problems. sdb is associated with higher mortality rates in infants with chd and continues to affect individuals throughout their lifespan and have major impacts on quality of life. several studies in children and adolescents with chd have demonstrated an association between poor sleep quality and decreased iq, memory, attention and adaptive functioning, as well as increased mood problems. additionally, chd and sleep disorders can both have profound adverse effects on caregivers and families. there is a paucity of research on caregiver stress and burden for caregivers of individuals with chd and sdb. sdb treatments represent a novel approach that may improve the cognitive, behavioral, and quality of life impairments well known to occur in individuals with chd. standard treatments for sdb like cpap or other non-invasive ventilatory modalities can be successful but may require modification for some forms of chd. for example, because of intrinsic preload dependence, individuals with fontan physiology are particularly sensitive to increases in pvr and may therefore require lower pressures during cpap therapy. given the complexity of treating sdb in individuals with chd, novel approaches may be particularly important for individuals with chd. recent studies have identified medication treatments including tirzepatide and the combination of atomoxetine and oxybutynin as novel osa treatments that may be particularly useful for a unique population that has unique physiologic risks limiting cpap treatment . however, there are limited existing data on any of these therapies specific to individuals with chd. the combination of atomoxetine and oxbutynin was studied in children with down syndrome and 73% of these children had comorbid chd. however other studies of novel osa treatments have not specifically included individuals with chd. interventional studies including individuals with chd would be valuable in showing whether these medications can serve as effective alternatives to cpap for people with chd. further research is needed on optimal treatment strategies for central sleep apnea or nocturnal hypoxemia. non-invasive ventilation (with the caveats previously noted) or oxygen may be reasonable approaches for central sleep apnea. oxygen may be safe and effective for central sleep apnea and nocturnal hypoxemia for many individuals with chd. however, oxygen may also lead to pulmonary overload in certain forms of chd, particularly unrepaired shunt lesions or palliated cyanotic defects. similarly, acetazolamide could be considered for central sleep apnea treatment but there is no published evidence for this specific to sdb treatment individuals with chd. given often critical balance of volume status for systemic cardiac output and pulmonary overload in individuals with chd and the diuretic effect of acetazolamide, this may also be contra-indicated for some individuals. finally, for many forms of chd, particularly prior to final repair, oxygen saturations below 88 or 90% are expected secondary to the chd lesion and right to left shunting of de-oxygenated blood. careful coordination with the individual's cardiologist is needed to avoid unintended consequences of sdb treatment. the existing literature highlights the importance of sdb in individuals with chd, however there are significant limitations to the existing literature and further work is needed. current literature is generally limited to only cross-sectional or observational studies. many studies included only a small number of participants. prospective longitudinal studies, ideally across multiple centers, are needed to further understand the impact of sdb on health, quality of life and neurodevelopment in individuals with chd and other sleep disorders on individuals with chd. such studies would also be an ideal opportunity to evaluate other sleep disorders as well, such as insomnia. existing studies of sdb have used heterogenous approaches to sdb diagnosis including questionnaires, home sleep tests and in-lab polysomnography. this is likely to explain some of the varied estimates of prevalence across studies and the utility of direct comparisons across studies in this review is limited due to this. consistent diagnostic testing, ideally with in-lab polysomnography would allow for a more accurate assessment of the differences in sdb prevalence across chd lesions and age groups. very few studies have more broadly evaluated sleep in individuals with chd, and these studies have not been designed from the ground up to evaluate sleep outcomes. most existing data for sleep disorders beyond sdb in people with chd have been done through secondary analysis of large studies, often with only a limited evaluation of sleep . there is no detailed rigorous broad assessment of sleep and associated impairments in individuals with chd. an ideal study may include objective sleep testing with polysomnography along with actigraphy or other measures of sleep timing, sleep duration, and perceived sleep quality. alternatively, a more rigorous assessment of sleep in chd studies not focused on sleep disorders would likely yield rich data at a very low cost. incorporating validated sleep questionnaires and a brief survey of sleep timing and duration would require only a few extra minutes from participants. overall, current evidence highlights that sdb appears to occur much more commercial use of this work, please see paragraphs 4.2 and 5 of our terms ( https://www.dovepress.com/terms.php ). introduction the rapid expansion of digital technology has increased adolescents' exposure to online risks, including cyberbullying victimization (cbv) and online gaming addiction (oga), which may be associated with self-harming behavior (shb). this study examined regional disparities in digital risk exposure and shb among indonesian adolescents. methods a cross-sectional study was conducted among 1742 adolescents aged 11-16 years from five regions of indonesia: sumatera, java, kalimantan, sulawesi, and papua. participants were recruited using multistage cluster sampling. data were collected using demographic questionnaires, the indonesian online game addiction questionnaire, the cyberbullying and online aggression survey instrument, and the self-harm inventory (shi). regional differences were examined using chi-square tests, and multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with lifetime shb. results the prevalence of lifetime shb was 55.0% and varied significantly across regions, ranging from 34.3% in java to 84.6% in sulawesi. oga and cbv were most prevalent in java (67.9% and 81.2%, respectively), followed by sulawesi. in adjusted analyses, adolescents in sulawesi had higher odds of lifetime shb, whereas those in java had lower odds compared with adolescents in papua. older age, male sex, longer internet use, and cbv were significantly associated with higher odds of lifetime shb, while oga was not significantly associated with shb. discussion regional differences in lifetime shb were not fully explained by digital risk exposure alone and may reflect broader psychosocial and contextual factors that warrant further investigation. these findings highlight the importance of considering regional context and cbv in adolescent shb prevention and mental health strategies. region-specific approaches addressing digital safety, psychosocial support, and equitable access to adolescent mental health services may be warranted. the widespread use of the internet, social media, and online gaming platforms has provided adolescents with opportunities for entertainment, social connection, and virtual interaction. 1 the united nations children's fund (unicef) further emphasized in 2023 that the internet has become an integral component of adolescents' daily lives, supporting educational activities, communication, entertainment, and skill development. 2 in indonesia, digital transformation has progressed rapidly, as reflected by increasing internet connectivity, smartphone ownership, and adolescents' high engagement in online activities. 3 adolescents represent one of the population groups with the highest internet penetration rates due to the integration of digital activities into everyday life. in the literature, problematic online gaming has been described using various terms, including internet gaming addiction (iga) or online gaming addiction (oga). although these terms overlap in describing problematic patterns of online gaming, terminology and operational definitions may vary across studies. cb refers to willful and repeated harm inflicted through the use of computers, cell phones, and other electronic devices. 5 oga refers to the persistent and recurrent use of the internet to engage in games that leads to significant impairment or distress in a person's life. 6 the rapid expansion of digital access among indonesian adolescents may therefore simultaneously create opportunities for social participation while also increasing exposure to online risks. 7 high levels of digital exposure among adolescents have been associated with a broad range of adverse mental health outcomes, including depression, anxiety, sleep disturbances, and reduced psychological well-being. 8 oga has also been associated with adverse mental health outcomes and reduced subjective well-being among adolescents. 9 in addition, cb has consistently been associated with depression, anxiety, suicidal ideation, and shb among adolescents. 10 emerging evidence suggests that excessive digital media use and harmful online experiences are associated with an increased risk of self-harm and related adverse outcomes among adolescents. 11 , 12 previous studies have suggested that adolescents who spend prolonged periods online, particularly on social media and across multiple platforms, are more likely to engage in shb. 13 online environments may facilitate exposure to self-harm-related content, social comparison, cyberbullying, and peer interactions that could contribute to psychological distress. similarly, longitudinal evidence has demonstrated that greater screen use is associated with subsequent risks of self-harm and suicidal behaviours among young people. 14 excessive or problematic internet use may also be associated with poorer sleep quality and sleep disturbances among adolescents, 15 which may contribute to psychological distress and vulnerability to shb. furthermore, both cb and problematic or addictive online gaming have been associated with shb among adolescents. 16 , 17 given its substantial impact on adolescent health, shb is the third leading cause of disability-adjusted life years (dalys) among adolescents. 18 psychological vulnerabilities such as impulsivity may further contribute to adolescents' vulnerability to shb. longitudinal evidence indicates that specific facets of impulsivity are differentially associated with the onset and maintenance of shb among young adolescents. 19 shb among adolescents is increasingly understood as a multifactorial phenomenon influenced not only by individual psychological vulnerabilities, but also by interpersonal, social, and environmental stressors, including experiences occurring within digital contexts. previous research has reported associations between cb and shb, as well as between internet addiction and subsequent shb or suicidal behaviour among adolescents. 16 , 20 the relationship between digital risk exposure and shb can be understood through the lens of emotion regulation theory. according to the process model of emotion regulation, individuals regulate emotional responses through processes involving situation selection, situation modification, attentional deployment, cognitive change, and response modulation. 21 from this perspective, adverse digital experiences such as cb may contribute to negative emotional states and psychological distress, which have been associated with increased vulnerability to shb. 16 similarly, problematic or addictive online gaming has been linked to difficulties in emotional regulation, including emotional suppression and negative escapism. 22 thus, difficulties in regulating negative emotional states may represent a potential pathway linking digital risk exposure with shb among adolescents. despite accumulating evidence linking digital risks to adverse mental health outcomes, previous research has primarily focused on individual-level associations, providing limited insight into how these risks and shb may vary across geographic and sociocultural contexts. existing studies have predominantly focused on individual-level associations and have generally been conducted in relatively homogeneous populations with high levels of digital connectivity, thereby providing limited insight into contextual and regional variations in adolescents' digital experiences. 1 as a result, the broader influence of structural and regional inequalities on adolescent digital vulnerability remains insufficiently understood. this is particularly relevant in archipelagic countries characterized by substantial regional disparities, such as indonesia. 23 this gap is particularly relevant in indonesia, an archipelagic country characterized by substantial regional differences in digital access, urbanization, socioeconomic conditions, educational resources, and mental health service availability. 24 , 25 these inequalities may shape patterns of internet use and influence adolescents' exposure to digital risks. social and cultural factors, including parental supervision, social support, and community norms, may also contribute to regional differences in adolescents' online experiences. 26 moreover, previous studies have demonstrated that adolescent mental health outcomes in indonesia vary according to geographic location and sociodemographic characteristics. 27 , 28 however, limited research has examined regional differences in oga, cb and shb simultaneously among adolescents across geographically diverse regions of the country. understanding these regional disparities is therefore essential for identifying contextual determinants of adolescent digital vulnerability and for developing geographically targeted mental health interventions. regional inequalities in indonesia may therefore contribute to unequal digital access and differing digital environments across regions. 29 , 30 the present study addresses this gap by examining regional disparities in shb among adolescents in relation to oga and cb across five major geographical regions of indonesia. by incorporating geographic context into the analysis, this study extends previous individual-level research and examines whether oga, cb, and shb vary across regional settings. these findings may contribute to a more context-sensitive understanding of adolescent digital risk exposure and shb and inform the development of regionally appropriate strategies for adolescent mental health promotion and prevention in indonesia. methods study design and setting this study employed a quantitative cross-sectional design using data collected from junior high school adolescents across five geographically diverse regions of indonesia. a cross-sectional design was considered appropriate for examining regional variations in cbv, oga, shb as well as the associations between these variables within a heterogeneous adolescent population. the study was conducted in five major regions of indonesia: sumatera, kalimantan, java, sulawesi, and papua. these regions were purposively selected to capture variations in geographic conditions, urbanization, socioeconomic background, digital infrastructure, and internet accessibility across indonesia. they also represent diverse sociocultural contexts and differing levels of technological development that may influence adolescents' digital experiences and behavioural patterns. participants and sampling procedures the study population comprised adolescents enrolled in schools across five indonesian provinces, namely jambi, west kalimantan, east java, north sulawesi, and central papua. the data analyzed in this study were collected as part of a broader school-based survey examining adolescent digital behaviours and mental health in indonesia. a multistage school-based sampling approach was used to recruit participants across the selected provinces. in the first stage, five provinces representing different geographical regions of indonesia were purposively selected to capture geographic variation across sumatera, kalimantan, java, sulawesi, and papua. the selection of study locations was guided by practical considerations, including research feasibility, site accessibility, and existing collaboration with local stakeholders. accordingly, the geographic coverage of the study was intended to support comparisons between the selected regions and should not be interpreted as a nationally representative sampling framework. in the second stage, schools were recruited with assistance from local education authorities in the respective study areas. in total, 26 junior high schools were invited to participate, and 22 schools subsequently took part in the study. based on school records, the participating schools reported a combined student enrollment of approximately 16,135 students. in the third stage, students attending the participating schools who met the study eligibility criteria were invited to participate. eligible participants were adolescents aged 10-19 years who were actively enrolled in the participating schools and capable of completing the study questionnaires independently. adolescents with cognitive impairments or health conditions that could interfere with independent questionnaire completion were not eligible for participation. of the 1768 eligible adolescents approached, 26 did not participate, yielding a final sample of 1742 adolescents for the present analysis. ethical approval for the study was obtained from the health research ethics committee of the faculty of medicine, universitas tanjungpura (approval no. 4200/un22.9/pt.0104/2025) prior to data collection. the regional distribution of participants was not based on proportional allocation according to the adolescent population size of each province. consequently, the number of participants differed between regions, which may influence the precision of regional estimates and should be considered when comparing findings across study locations. in addition, because the number of students who initially received or accessed the questionnaires was not systematically documented, a precise overall participation rate could not be established. because the present study analyzed data collected as part of a broader school-based survey, an a priori sample size or statistical power calculation was not performed specifically for the present analysis. all eligible respondents from the broader survey were included in the present analysis. data collection procedures data were collected between june and july 2025 using both online and paper-based questionnaires, depending on internet availability at participating schools. online questionnaires were administered in schools with adequate internet connectivity, whereas paper-based questionnaires were used in schools located in areas with limited or unreliable internet access. before data collection, informed consent was obtained from parents or legal guardians, and assent was obtained from adolescent participants, as applicable. participants were informed about the voluntary nature of participation and their right to withdraw from the study without consequences. the questionnaires were completed anonymously, and no personally identifiable information was collected. data collection procedures were supervised by the principal investigator to ensure consistent administration across participating schools and regions. measures participant characteristics were assessed using a demographic questionnaire that collected information on age, sex, and estimated daily internet use duration. age was recorded in years and presented as a categorical variable in the descriptive analysis, ranging from 11 to 16 years. oga was assessed using the indonesian online game addiction questionnaire developed by jap et al 31 the instrument comprises seven items rated on a five-point likert scale, yielding total scores ranging from 7 to 35, with higher scores reflecting greater problematic involvement in online gaming. an example item is, "i think about online games all day long". this dichotomization was applied for the purposes of statistical analysis and does not alter the original three-category classification. the instrument has demonstrated satisfactory internal consistency, with a reported cronbach's alpha of 0.73. cb exposure was assessed using the nine-item cyberbullying victimization scale developed by hinduja and patchin. 5 the instrument assesses adolescents' experiences of being targeted by cyberbullying during the preceding 30 days. although the broader assessment included measures of both cbv and cb perpetration, the present analysis focused specifically on the victimization component. one example item is, "i have been cyberbullied". responses are rated on a four-point frequency scale ranging from never (0) to many times (3). item scores are summed to yield a total victimization score ranging from 0 to 27, with higher scores indicating more frequent experiences of cbv. the scale has demonstrated good internal consistency in previous studies, with reported cronbach's alpha coefficients ranging from 0.867 to 0.935. accordingly, the present analysis examined cbv only and did not include cb perpetration in the regression models. shb was assessed using the self-harm inventory (shi) developed by sansone et al. 32 the shi comprises 22 items assessing lifetime engagement in various shb, with each item requiring a dichotomous yes/no response. an example item is, "have you ever intentionally, or on purpose, cut yourself?" each affirmative response is assigned a score of 1 and each negative response a score of 0, resulting in a total score ranging from 0 to 22. higher scores indicate a greater number of shb endorsed by the respondent. previous research has demonstrated satisfactory psychometric properties of the indonesian version of the shi, including good internal consistency (cronbach's alpha = 0.831). 33 in the present study, shb was operationalized as a binary variable based on lifetime history. data analysis data analysis focused on examining regional disparities in digital risk exposure and shb among adolescents. all statistical analyses were performed using ibm spss statistics version 19.0. descriptive statistics were used to summarize participant characteristics and describe the prevalence of oga, cbv, and shb across the five study regions. pearson's chi-square tests were used to examine differences in categorical variables across regions. for the multivariable logistic regression analysis, shb was coded as a binary outcome (0 = no shb; 1 = shb). categorical predictors were dummy-coded, with the following reference categories: female for sex, 3 hours/day for internet use duration, no gaming addiction for gaming addiction, no cyberbullying victimization for cyberbullying, and papua for region. sex, internet use duration, oga, and cbv were coded as binary variables (0 = reference category; 1 = comparison category). region was entered as a categorical variable using papua as the reference category, with dummy variables representing sumatera, java, kalimantan, and sulawesi. age was entered as a continuous variable. adjusted odds ratios (aors) greater than 1 indicated higher odds of shb relative to the reference category, whereas aors less than 1 indicated lower odds. for age, the aor represented the odds ratio associated with a one-year increase in age. multicollinearity among predictors was assessed using tolerance and variance inflation factor (vif) statistics. model fit was assessed using the hosmer-lemeshow goodness-of-fit test. the analysis included 1742 participants, with no missing cases in the variables included in the regression model. because the primary analyses were conducted using conventional statistical procedures, clustering of participants within schools was not explicitly accounted for in the statistical models. ethical considerations this study received ethical approval from the health research ethics committee of the faculty of medicine, universitas tanjungpura (approval no. all procedures were conducted in accordance with the declaration of helsinki (2013) and the cioms international ethical guidelines (2016). results a total of 1742 adolescents from five regions of indonesia were included in the analysis ( table 1 ). adolescents aged 13-15 years constituted the majority of participants across all regions. the proportion of male participants was highest in sumatera (66.9%) and kalimantan (61.4%), whereas female participants predominated in java (72.3%) and sulawesi (70.1%). the prevalence of oga and cbv varied significantly across regions ( table 2 ). oga was most prevalent among adolescents in java (67.9%) and sulawesi (63.6%), whereas the lowest prevalence was observed in sumatera (10.1%). cbv was also highest in java (81.2%) and sulawesi (75.2%), compared with the lowest prevalence in kalimantan (32.6%). the prevalence of lifetime shb also varied substantially by region ( table 3 ). the highest prevalence was observed in sulawesi (84.6%), followed by sumatera (62.0%), kalimantan (59.1%), and papua (53.6%), while java had the lowest prevalence (34.3%). the regional difference in lifetime shb was statistically significant (p 0.001). in the adjusted logistic regression model ( table 4 ), significant regional disparities in lifetime shb remained evident after controlling for age, sex, internet duration, oga, and cbv. compared with adolescents in papua, those in sulawesi had higher odds of lifetime shb (aor = 3.718, 95% ci: 2.423-5.705, p 0.001), whereas those in java had lower odds (aor = 0.276, 95% ci: 0.201-0.380, p 0.001). oga not significantly associated with lifetime shb after adjustment (aor = 1.024, 95% ci: 0.762-1.375, p = 0.875). abbreviations : b, regression coefficient; se, standard error; or, odds ratio; ci, confidence interval; oga, online gaming addiction; cbv, cyberbullying victimization. discussion this study revealed a high prevalence of lifetime self-harming behavior (shb) among indonesian adolescents, with significant regional variations. this pattern suggests that geographic and regional social contexts may shape adolescents' vulnerability to shb. previous studies have demonstrated that adolescent mental health problems and shb in indonesia are associated with disparities in social conditions, economic resources, and healthcare accessibility across regions. one study reported variations in adolescent mental health problems between urban and more remote areas in indonesia, which were associated with unequal availability of resources and mental health services. 28 adolescents living in areas with limited healthcare facilities experience greater barriers to accessing mental health services due to stigma, inadequate mental health literacy, and shortages of mental health professionals. 34 the relatively high prevalence of cyberbullying victimization (cbv) observed in this study should be interpreted in light of the measurement and classification approach used. although the broader assessment included both cbv and perpetration, the present analysis focused specifically on victimization during the preceding 30 days. therefore, the prevalence estimates reflect recent cbv based on the study-specific cutoff and should not be interpreted as measures of cb perpetration or as combined estimates of victimization and perpetration. interestingly, the regional pattern observed in this study did not fully correspond with the distribution of digital risk factors. although adolescents in java had the highest prevalence of online game addiction (oga) and cbv, they showed the lowest prevalence of lifetime shb. in contrast, sulawesi had the highest prevalence of shb and substantially higher adjusted odds of shb than papua. these findings suggest that regional disparities in shb cannot be fully explained by digital risk exposure alone and may reflect the influence of broader contextual factors. previous studies have reported that geographic variations in shb are associated with socio-economic deprivation and social fragmentation. 35 moreover, shb has been associated with socio-economic conditions at both the individual and community levels, with material and social deprivation contributing to higher rates of self-harm hospitalization. 36 the relatively high prevalence of lifetime shb observed in this study should also be interpreted in the context of the measurement approach. therefore, the prevalence estimate reflects lifetime engagement in any of the shb assessed by the shi and should not be interpreted as an estimate of current or recent shb. the broad coverage of lifetime shb and the use of a threshold of at least one endorsed behaviour may partly contribute to the relatively high prevalence observed in this study. differences in measurement approaches, study populations, and other methodological factors may also contribute to variation in reported shb prevalence across studies. 37 , 38 a key finding of this study was that adolescents in sulawesi had approximately 3.7-fold higher adjusted odds of lifetime shb than those in papua, whereas adolescents in java had significantly lower odds. the contrasting regional patterns observed in this study warrant further consideration. java had the highest prevalence of both oga and cbv, yet adolescents in java had the lowest prevalence of lifetime shb and significantly lower adjusted odds of shb than those in papua. in contrast, sulawesi had a lower prevalence of oga and cbv than java, but had the highest prevalence of lifetime shb and the highest adjusted odds of shb compared with papua. this pattern suggests that the relationship between digital risk exposure and shb may not be linear or directly proportional at the regional level. these regional differences may be related to variations in broader psychosocial, social, and contextual factors across indonesian regions, although these factors were not directly assessed in the present study. variations in socioeconomic conditions may contribute to differences in adolescents' vulnerability to shb, as lower parental socioeconomic position has been associated with a higher risk of shb among adolescents. 39 furthermore, family relationship quality, school connectedness, and supportive community environments have been identified as important protective factors against adolescent shb. 40 thus, high digital risk exposure alone may not necessarily correspond to higher shb prevalence at the regional level. these findings highlight the importance of interpreting regional disparities in adolescent shb within a broader ecological framework rather than attributing them solely to individual-level digital risk factors. because these contextual factors were not directly measured in the present study, they should be considered as potential explanations or hypotheses for future research rather than established causes of the observed regional differences. the persistence of regional differences after adjustment for age, sex, internet use duration, oga, and cbv suggests that factors beyond individual-level digital experiences may contribute to regional disparities in adolescent shb. previous longitudinal research has identified multiple developmental pathways to adolescent self-harm involving emotional difficulties, bullying, family-related challenges, peer relationships, and risk-taking behaviours, highlighting the potential relevance of broader psychosocial contexts. 41 however, these contextual factors were not directly measured in the present study and should therefore be considered potential explanations that warrant further investigation. age was also significantly associated with lifetime shb, with each one-year increase in age associated with approximately 43% higher odds of shb. this finding is consistent with previous evidence indicating that middle to late adolescence represents a critical developmental period for the emergence of shb. this finding is consistent with previous evidence indicating that adolescence represents a critical developmental period for the emergence of self-harm. a recent scoping review of children and adolescents reported that the age of self-harm onset ranged from 9 to 18 years, with most studies reporting a mean onset age between 12 and 14 years, 42 whereas shb occur most frequently among adolescents aged 14-17 years. 19 these findings reinforce the notion that middle and late adolescence are developmental stages characterized by heightened emotional and behavioural vulnerability. such vulnerability may be attributable to the complex biological, psychological, and social transitions occurring during adolescence. a study demonstrated that adolescents with poor emotion regulation, low self-esteem, bullying experiences, and chronic emotional distress are more likely to engage in self-harm. 43 similarly, previous study found that social pressure, bullying, and limited social support were significantly associated with shb among adolescents. 44 these findings support the theoretical perspective that heightened sensitivity to interpersonal stressors during adolescence may intensify emotional distress and increase vulnerability to shb. furthermore, difficulties in adaptively regulating negative emotions may represent an important mechanism underlying shb. shb is frequently used as a maladaptive emotion regulation strategy to temporarily alleviate negative affect and psychological tension. 19 this interpretation further supports the possibility that shb may emerge as a coping response to unresolved emotional distress during adolescence. after adjustment for other covariates, male adolescents had 1.51 times the odds of lifetime shb compared with female adolescents, corresponding to approximately 51% higher odds. this finding contrasts with global burden of disease estimates, which reported higher incidence and years lived with disability due to adolescent self-harm among females than males, although males showed higher disability-adjusted life years. 45 existing evidence has also indicated that females are more likely to exhibit internalizing symptoms, including depression, anxiety, and emotional dysregulation, whereas males more commonly display externalizing behaviours such as aggression and risk-taking. previous study identified interpersonal stress and risky behavior as important developmental pathways leading to adolescent shb. 43 the persistence of regional differences after adjustment for age, sex, internet use duration, oga, and cbv suggests that factors beyond individual-level digital experiences may contribute to regional disparities in adolescent shb. previous behaviours, highlighting the potential relevance of broader psychosocial contexts. 41 however, these contextual factors were not directly measured in the present study and should therefore be considered potential explanations that warrant further investigation. the higher odds observed among male adolescents in the present study may therefore reflect differences in emotional coping, help-seeking patterns, social expectations, or the expression of psychological distress across sexes. however, these mechanisms were not directly assessed in this study and warrant further investigation. internet use duration was also significantly associated with lifetime shb after adjustment for covariates. this finding is consistent with longitudinal evidence showing that excessive internet use is associated with an increased risk of subsequent self-harm among adolescents. 12 similarly, adolescents who spend more time using digital media, particularly the internet, have been reported to have a higher likelihood of self-harm, although these associations may differ by sex. 46 taken together, these findings suggest that the association between internet use duration and shb may involve multiple interrelated emotional, behavioural, and psychosocial mechanisms. however, because the present study did not assess the specific types or purposes of internet use, further cyberbullying had increased odds of subsequent self-harm one year later, even after adjustment for key covariates. 47 similarly, a cross-sectional study among adolescents from diverse urban schools in the importance of considering cbv in the identification and prevention of shb among adolescents. in contrast to cbv, oga was not significantly associated with lifetime shb after adjustment for several strengths. first, the inclusion of adolescents from geographically diverse regions of indonesia enabled the examination of regional disparities in shb alongside digital risk factors. second, the use of multivariable statistical analyses allowed the associations between regional context, demographic characteristics, and digital risk factors to be examined simultaneously. by integrating geographic context, individual characteristics, and digital behavioural factors within a single analytical framework, this study contributes to a more comprehensive understanding of factors associated with shb among indonesian adolescents. the findings provide preliminary evidence that regional disparities in shb may not be fully explained by individual-level digital risk exposure alone, highlighting the importance of considering broader psychosocial and contextual factors in adolescent mental health research and prevention. several limitations should be considered when interpreting the findings. first, the cross-sectional design and the available measures did not allow the frequency, persistence, or temporal sequence of cbv and shb to be established. therefore, the direction of the observed association and the time interval between cbv and shb remain uncertain. second, reliance on self-reported measures may have introduced reporting bias, including recall and social desirability biases. third, data were collected using both online and paper-based questionnaires, depending on internet availability at participating schools. differences in survey mode may have influenced the reporting of sensitive behaviours, including shb and cbv and may have contributed to variation in disclosure across settings. because survey mode was determined by school-level internet accessibility rather than experimental assignment, the potential influence of survey mode on participants' responses could not be directly evaluated. fourth, clustering of participants within schools was not explicitly accounted for in the statistical analyses. as adolescents from the same school may share similar social and environmental characteristics, potential within-school clustering may have affected the precision of the estimated associations. fifth, the distribution of participants across regions was not balanced, with some regions having substantially larger samples than others. this imbalance may have affected the precision of regional prevalence estimates and reduced the comparability of estimates across regions with different sample sizes. therefore, regional differences should be interpreted cautiously, particularly when comparing estimates from regions with smaller sample sizes, and the findings should not be considered nationally representative of adolescents in each region. sixth, the relatively high prevalence estimates observed in this study compared with some previous reports may partly reflect differences in operational definitions, measurement instruments, and cultural contexts. in particular, the shi assesses lifetime history of self-harm behaviours and includes a broad range of self-harm behaviours, which may partly contribute to the relatively high prevalence observed in the present study. differences in the operationalization and measurement of cyberbullying victimization across studies may also contribute to variation in reported prevalence estimates. finally, several potential psychological and contextual mechanisms underlying the observed associations, including emotion regulation, family support, and psychosocial protective factors, were not directly assessed. therefore, these factors should be considered possible explanations rather than established mechanisms, and the pathways linking regional and digital risk factors to shb remain uncertain. future research directions future research should employ more balanced sampling strategies to improve the precision and generalizability of regional comparisons. longitudinal designs are needed to clarify the temporal relationships between digital risk factors and shb and to better examine potential causal pathways. such research may provide a stronger basis for understanding the mechanisms underlying regional disparities in adolescent shb and for developing context-sensitive prevention and intervention strategies across different regions of indonesia. conclusion this cross-sectional study found significant regional differences in lifetime shb among indonesian adolescents, with these differences remaining after adjustment for demographic characteristics and measured digital risk factors. older age, male sex, longer internet use duration, and cbv were significantly associated with higher odds of lifetime shb, whereas oga was not independently associated with shb after adjustment. however, the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, and the use of self-reported measures and different survey modes may have influenced the reporting of sensitive behaviours. the unequal distribution of participants across regions and the non-representative sampling also limit the comparability and generalizability of regional estimates. the observed regional patterns should therefore be interpreted cautiously and should not be interpreted as evidence of causal regional effects. potential psychosocial, socioeconomic, family, school, community, and healthcare-related factors underlying these regional differences were not directly assessed and should therefore be considered possible explanations rather than established causes. future longitudinal studies using more balanced and representative sampling and standardized measurement approaches are needed to further investigate the factors underlying regional differences in adolescent shb. acknowledgments this publication charge is funded by unpad through the indonesian endowment fund for education (lpdp) on behalf of the indonesian ministry of antibodies in cerebrospinal fluid (csf). methods we retrospectively reviewed all patients with csf-confirmed anti-nmdar encephalitis at the second affiliated hospital of guangzhou medical university between 2016 and 2025. collected data included initial symptoms and disease severity, csf and serum test results, magnetic resonance imaging (mri) and neuro-electrophysiological findings, primary
